_note: Hand-written fixture, not a recorded model response. Every case must be flagged by IdentifierEchoDetector with the listed reason. Reasons are checked in order: title_is_identifier, title_identifier_share, summary_identifier_share, summary_copied; the first hit wins.

detector_spec.comparison: Every ratio rule uses strict greater-than. A ratio equal to its threshold passes.
detector_spec.tokenize: Split title or summary on whitespace. From each raw token trim leading chars in [" ' ` ( [ { < “ ‘]. Then repeatedly trim one trailing char while it is in [" ' ` , ; : ! ? . ] } > ” ’], or it is ')' and the token does not end with '()'. Keep tokens that contain at least one letter or digit (word tokens). The share denominator is the count of all word tokens; no stopword list.
identifierShape: call: ends with '()' and has a letter before it
camel hump: a lowercase letter immediately followed by an uppercase letter (ExecuteAsync, maxBytes, GitHub)
snake: contains '_' and at least one letter (split_into_batches)
screaming: [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(_[A-Z0-9]+)+ (already covered by snake; listed for clarity). Plain all-caps words such as HTTP, JSON, API are NOT identifier-shaped
dot path: contains a match of [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)+ with at least one segment of 2 or more chars. Excludes e.g, i.e, U.S; numbers like 3.2 never match
detector_spec.presence: A token is an echo identifier when it is identifier-shaped AND present in the ORIGINAL unit.Text: strip a trailing '()' then ordinal (case-sensitive) Contains. For a dot path that is not found whole, it is present when every '.'-separated segment is found by ordinal Contains (catches composed Class.Method titles).
rules: title_is_identifier: the title has exactly 1 word token and it is an echo identifier
title_identifier_share: echo identifiers / title word tokens > TitleEchoRatio
summary_identifier_share: echo identifiers / summary word tokens > SummaryEchoRatio

summary_copied: normalize summary and unit.Text (ToLowerInvariant, collapse whitespace runs to one space, trim); if normalized summary length >= MinCopyCheckLength and longest common substring (characters) / normalized summary length > SummaryCopyRatio
detector_spec.scope: Only title and summary are checked. details and anchor_quote are never checked (anchor_quote is meant to be verbatim; details may hold up to 2 backticked identifiers).
detector_spec.lcsNote: Summary is at most 2000 chars but unit text can be long; use a suffix automaton over the unit text or rolling-hash binary search rather than a full O(n*m) table.

MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 50


def split_into_batches(documents, max_bytes):
    """Group documents so each batch stays under both the count and size limits."""
    batches, current, current_bytes = [], [], 0
    for doc in documents:
        size = len(doc.payload)
        if current and (len(current) == MAX_BATCH_SIZE or current_bytes + size > max_bytes):
            batches.append(current)
            current, current_bytes = [], 0
        current.append(doc)
        current_bytes += size
    if current:
        batches.append(current)
    return batches

cases.unit_text:
4 Incremental Indexing
Our approach builds the index incrementally. Instead of rebuilding the full inverted index after every update, new documents are written to a small in-memory segment that is merged into the main index once it exceeds a size threshold. This keeps write latency low while bounding the number of segments a query must scan.
In our experiments the merge threshold of 64 MB gave the best balance between write throughput and query latency (see Table 2).
